stop_condition: every round-2 finding (R2-F1..F4) is verified fixed by independent measurement rather than by the fix round's claim; both new mutation pairings (C11, C12) are rebuilt from the current tree and shown to fail for the right reason; the R2-F3 refusal's escape hatch is exercised end to end; and no HIGH or critical remains in the guards, the force/validate ordering, or the shipped-invariant greps

findings.evidence:
THE MUTANT REPRODUCES THE PRE-FIX NUMBERS BY A MECHANISM UNRELATED TO THE GUARD. The awk-stripped region WOB2-R2F2-FORCE-BEFORE-VALIDATE (codex-review.sh:377-384) contains not only the force but the SOLE WRITE of $WORK/candidate.json -- the `else printf '%s' "$text" > "$WORK/candidate.json"` arm. You cannot strip a subset of an if/else and get valid bash, so the awk delete removes the write too. The stripped copy therefore calls validate-artifact on a file that is never written: measured directly, `review-check.sh validate-artifact <nonexistent>` returns {"ok":false,"error_key":"usage","observations":"file not found: ..."} rc=1. So validate_candidate returns 1 with error_key=invalid_json (the `// "invalid_json"` default) for EVERY input.

MEASURED, mutants rebuilt by me from the current tree (not the spec's copies), 16 candidate shapes x 3 drivers, production malformed_retry=1, shipped stub:
  - SPEC C11 MUTANT: rc=5 / 2 turns / no artifact on ALL SIXTEEN shapes -- including shape 00, a PERFECTLY VALID candidate whose reviewed_hash IS $REQ_CSH, and shape 04 (well-formed-but-wrong hash) which the TRUE pre-fix code ACCEPTS at rc=0 / 1 turn.
  - CORRECTLY-SCOPED MUTANT (region replaced by the pre-fix statement `printf '%s' "$text" > "$WORK/candidate.json"`, i.e. byte-equivalent to HEAD's validate_candidate; bash -n clean): rc=0 on shapes 00 and 04, rc=5 on the 11 malformed shapes. It DISCRIMINATES. The spec's does not.
So the three C11 META assertions ("WITHOUT the pre-force, the SAME malformed input now fails (exit 5)", "...it cost TWO paid turns", "...NO artifact was written") are satisfied by a mutant that is simply broken, and would be satisfied by it whatever input it received.

AGAINST THE STANDARD: .claude/tests/README.md pairing part 2 requires "an assertion that the mutant fails IN THE WAY THE GUARD PREVENTS, naming the check that would fail". This mutant fails via `usage`/file-not-found, never via reviewed_hash_unusable. The README's own worked example, approve-idempotency.sh F3, is cited there as including "a discriminator that rules out the wrong-reason block" -- that leg is exactly what C11 lacks. Part 1 (non-vacuity) IS satisfied: the strip lands, assert_mutant_applied fires, bash -n passes.

WHY THIS IS RECORDED AT MEDIUM AND NOT AS A BLOCK. The guard itself is load-bearing and I proved it independently (the correctly-scoped mutant above). The C11 DIRECT legs are sound and carry the real regression protection: reverting the fix properly turns them red (shipped rc=0 vs correct-pre-fix rc=5 on the identical truncated-63 input). I enumerated the realistic regressions -- neutering $REQ_CSH in the force, moving the force back after validation while keeping the write, deleting the region outright -- and the direct legs catch all three. So no coverage hole exists; what is defective is the strength of one proof, and the correct proof is now in this artifact and the qa-plan.
findings.description:
Two remedies, either sufficient; (b) is test-only and is the one I have already demonstrated works.

(a) PREFERRED, restructure so the sentinel region contains ONLY the force. Move the unconditional write ABOVE the START sentinel and make the region a single conditional overwrite, e.g.
      printf '%s' "$text" > "$WORK/candidate.json"
      # WOB2-R2F2-FORCE-BEFORE-VALIDATE-START
      forced=$(jq -c --arg csh "$REQ_CSH" '.reviewed_hash=$csh' "$WORK/candidate.json" 2>/dev/null) \
          && [ -n "$forced" ] && printf '%s' "$forced" > "$WORK/candidate.json"
      # WOB2-R2F2-FORCE-BEFORE-VALIDATE-END
    The existing awk delete then leaves exactly the pre-fix code, and C11's META becomes a true before/after pair with no test change at all.

(b) TEST-ONLY. Change the C11 mutation from an awk DELETE to an awk SUBSTITUTE that replaces the region with the pre-fix statement (the README explicitly contemplates sed/awk substitution as a mutation form: "a `sed` that substituted nothing" is called out as the failure to guard against, not substitution itself). Then add the missing discriminator leg: assert the mutant's recorded error_key is reviewed_hash_unusable and NOT `usage`, and add a leg asserting the mutant still SUCCEEDS on a valid candidate -- which is what rules out the wrong-reason block.

Whichever is chosen, C11's own assertion TEXT should stop claiming "the pre-fix defect returns" until the mutant actually reproduces the pre-fix behaviour rather than the pre-fix exit code.

findings.location: .claude/tests/component/specs/codex-review.sh:777,813 (the two new SC2034 sites); the fix round completion record payload_sha=aa55f3f0 llm_observations
findings.evidence:
The load-bearing half of the disclosure is EXACTLY RIGHT and I confirmed it independently: shellcheck 0.11.0 -f gcc --severity=warning, per-file, over the 8 L2 files outside make lint's glob, worktree vs a clean `git archive HEAD` tree -- 7 findings at HEAD, 9 in the worktree, and after stripping line numbers the set difference is exactly TWO, both SC2034 "appears unused": MUT_OUT (codex-review.sh:777) and C12_OUT (codex-review.sh:813). Nothing was removed. So "+2 net new, both SC2034, both mine" is correct and the round-1 "zero net new" framing is correctly retired.

Two attribution slips inside that disclosure, neither load-bearing:
  1. "5 of the 9 are line-shifted duplicates" -- measured FOUR shifted, three same-line. Shifted: fixture.sh SC2164 824->855, codex-review.sh REVIEW_CONFIG 544->583, review-bypass-anchor OUT8 491->505 and RC9 563->577. Unmoved: fixture.sh BD_ID_RE 273->273, review-artifact-durability 386->386 and 388->388.
  2. "the same capture-but-discard idiom already present unaddressed 3x in this exact file (OUT8, RC9, REVIEW_CONFIG)" -- only REVIEW_CONFIG is in codex-review.sh. OUT8 and RC9 are in review-bypass-anchor.sh, a sibling spec. So it is 1x in that file and 2x in the corpus, not 3x in that file.

DOES IT MATTER: no. All 8 files are genuinely outside the enforced glob (Makefile lint target; `make lint` rc=0 confirmed at this tree), the idiom is pre-existing, and I read the surrounding assertions -- neither MUT_OUT nor C12_OUT has content worth asserting, because in both legs the mutant/driver writes no artifact so stdout is empty. Recorded so the corrected numbers are the ones that survive, not to ask for work.

METHOD NOTE ON MY OWN FIGURES: my first attempt at this measurement returned 0 findings at both HEAD and worktree. That was a harness artifact -- an unquoted $FILES under zsh, which does not word-split, so shellcheck received one bogus argument and errored with stderr discarded. Re-run per-file under bash. Reporting it because it is the same shape of error the brief warned about.
findings.description: Corrected counts for the record: 4 line-shifted (not 5), and the sibling idiom is 1x in codex-review.sh plus 2x in review-bypass-anchor.sh (not 3x in codex-review.sh). The +2/SC2034/MUT_OUT+C12_OUT conclusion stands unchanged. No action requested.

findings.location: .gitattributes:3 (merge=beads registered for .beads/issues.jsonl only) vs .beads/interactions.jsonl (tracked, no driver)
findings.evidence:
DISCOVERED DURING THIS REVIEW, PRE-EXISTING, OUT OF SCOPE FOR wob2 -- filed as its own task per CONTRIBUTING.md rather than as a comment here.

.gitattributes registers the beads merge driver for ONE path: `.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads`. `.beads/interactions.jsonl` is ALSO tracked (git ls-files confirms; .beads/.gitignore's closing NOTE names it explicitly as intentionally tracked) and is ALSO an append-only, time-ordered JSONL -- but it has no merge driver. Two branches that both append will produce raw EOF conflict markers where the sibling file would merge cleanly.

Never actually observed: `git log --merges -- .beads/interactions.jsonl` = 0, because this history is linear. The risk is latent, not active. Remedy is one line in .gitattributes.

Searched before filing (the brief records two duplicate filings this session): no task matches on title or description for gitattributes / merge driver / merge=beads; claude-workflow-plugin-z0wx mentions interactions.jsonl but is a different defect (enter leaving a prior-cycle qa-approved in place).
findings.description: Answers the operator question directly: interactions.jsonl IS appropriate to commit -- tracking is deliberate documented policy (.beads/.gitignore names it), it has been committed in 32 commits including the last five consecutive, and it is NOT in the bound change set (0 in changed-files.txt, absent from the impact report 20 files), so this approval attests nothing about it. The separable real gap is the missing merge driver; filed as its own task.

findings.evidence:
qa.md:423 and review-check.sh's own refusal message both name the audited exit as `qa-gate.sh approve --no-review '<reason>'`. Exercised end to end in an isolated component fixture (real `bd init` in a tempdir, never the live store), that exact command is REFUSED first: rc=2, error_key=no_design_attempted, because cmd_approve's design precondition is evaluated before the review one. The call only succeeds as `approve <tid> --no-design '<reason>' --no-review '<reason>' '<summary>'`.

So the documented one-flag form is incomplete for the ordinary task -- the same shape the J21 escalation note already carries for `choose approve` ("on the ordinary task, no design phase at all: no_design_attempted"). The escape hatch itself WORKS and is not a dead end (see the qa-plan for the full transcript: rc=0, status=approved, and the record carries change_set_hash=e3b0c442..., reviewed_by=none, [review bypass: ...], [design bypass: ...]).

Recorded as INFO because the refusal is self-documenting -- it names --no-design and prints the corrected command -- so an operator following it is one read away from the right invocation. Worth one clause at qa.md:423 next time that paragraph is touched.
findings.description: One clause next time that paragraph is touched: on a task with no design phase the audited exit is `approve <tid> --no-design <reason> --no-review <reason> <summary>`. Not blocking -- the refusal names --no-design and prints the corrected command.
